_comment: Machine-readable rule catalog and regression cases. cases.md is the human-readable counterpart; the ids in both must correspond one-to-one (enforced by scripts/check_consistency.py). Use scripts/run_cases.py to validate and score.

R-EDITION-ORACLE.desc: Community Edition + Oracle mode must be rejected

R-KEY-3BRANCH.desc: The relationship between the partition key and the primary key/unique key is a three-branch conditional rule; having neither a primary key nor a unique key is valid

R-KEY-AUTOSPLIT-PREFIX.desc: Automatic partition splitting requires a primary key, with the partition key as a prefix of the primary key

R-UK-GLOBAL.desc: A unique index that does not cover all partition key columns must be upgraded to a global unique index, with the cost explained

R-ORACLE-NO-KEY.desc: Oracle mode has no PARTITION BY KEY

R-ORACLE-NO-COLUMNS.desc: Oracle mode has no COLUMNS keyword

R-MYSQL-NO-INTERVAL.desc: MySQL mode has no INTERVAL partitioning

R-PKEY-TYPE.desc: In MySQL mode, RANGE/LIST/HASH partition keys must be integer or YEAR type; RANGE/LIST are limited to a single column

R-LIST-ENUM-SYNTAX.desc: LIST enumeration uses VALUES IN(...) in MySQL mode and VALUES(...) in Oracle mode

R-LIST-DEFAULT.desc: LIST partitioning should include a DEFAULT fallback partition

R-MAXPART.desc: The per-table partition count limit is evaluated **per partitioned object** (the main table plus each independently-partitioned global index); the limit depends on the mode: MySQL = max_partition_num (default 8192, range [8192, 65536]), Oracle = fixed at 65536, this parameter is not used

R-AUTOSPLIT-LIMITS.desc: The ten official restrictions on automatic partition splitting

R-AUTOSPLIT-TRIGGER.desc: The SIZE threshold is determined by auto_split_tablet_size and requires enable_auto_split

R-TG-NONE-VERSION.desc: The risk assessment for SHARDING=NONE branches at V4.4.2 BP1, with interception in both directions

R-TG-SCOPE-VERSION.desc: Table Group SCOPE requires >= V4.4.2 BP1; lower versions get an alternative

R-DUPLICATE-TABLE.desc: For a large table joining a small dimension table, prefer a duplicated table; do not force a Table Group

R-CG-SEMANTICS.desc: Pure columnstore uses each column; all columns, each column is row+column redundancy, roughly 2x storage

R-SKIPINDEX.desc: Low-frequency/narrow multi-dimensional full-table aggregation uses row storage + SKIP_INDEX

R-CS-REPLICA-TOPOLOGY.desc: The columnstore replica is a deployment topology decision; a Hint cannot specify the replica type

R-STORAGE-AXES.desc: Storage decisions have two axes; isolation_required is evaluated first and must not be short-circuited by axis 1

R-QUEUING.desc: High-insert, high-delete tables are identified as queuing tables; recommend TABLE_MODE=QUEUING

R-TABLET-SUM.desc: Tablet count is summed across physical objects, including local and global indexes

R-TABLET-MIN-PERNODE.desc: The limit is min(A, B), compared on a per-node basis

R-NOORDER.desc: The sole criterion for NOORDER is that the business does not require strict monotonic increase; there is no TPS or partitioned-table precondition

R-GI-COST.desc: A global index is a cost decision, not a forbidden zone

R-GI-DROPPART.desc: Adding a global index to an archive table requires flagging the rebuild cost of DROP PARTITION

R-HOTSPOT-TYPES.desc: Hotspots are first classified by read/write direction, then into five types; sub-partitioning cannot break up a single-key hotspot

R-MULTI-DIM.desc: When multiple high-frequency dimensions conflict, output a trade-off rather than rejecting the design

R-INPUT-QUANT.desc: Quantified inputs: if missing, request them or mark as unverified; never fabricate them

R-L2-NO-REJECT.desc: L2 empirical thresholds must not be used to reject a design

R-EVIDENCE.desc: Without evidence, must not output pass; only unverified is allowed

R-VERSION-GATE.desc: When the version is below the feature requirement, reject and provide an alternative

R-AUTOINC-PKEY.desc: Using an auto-increment column as the partition key causes cross-node transactions; must be flagged

R-CONFIRMED-DDL-ONLY.desc: The main DDL may only use C1 confirmed capabilities; C2/C3 must go into candidate_ddl — marking as unverified does not count as compliant

R-TABLET-WORST-NODE.desc: Capacity assessment for heterogeneous Zones/Units must use the worst-case node, not the average

R-AUTOINC-MODE-GATE.desc: AUTO_INCREMENT / AUTO_INCREMENT_MODE apply only to MySQL mode; Oracle mode uses IDENTITY or a sequence

R-TENANT-DEFAULT-FORMAT.desc: When no Column Group is specified, the actual storage format is determined by the tenant parameter default_table_store_format; it must not be asserted to be row storage

R-NDV-GT-PARTITIONS.desc: The cardinality of a HASH/KEY partition key should exceed the number of partitions (L1-B design blocker, NOT L0: the statement is legal, so the DDL is still emitted with the empty-partition count quantified); when distinct_count is missing, this is unverified

R-HTAP-FOUR-TIERS.desc: HTAP has four tiers of storage architecture; columnstore indexes/row-store indexes are C3 and may only go into candidate_ddl

R-TABLEMODE-COMPACTION.desc: The difference among the five TABLE_MODE values is how aggressively major compaction is triggered, not "queue intensity"

R-HOTSPOT-READ-DIRECTION.desc: Hotspots must first be classified by read/write direction; read hotspots should use duplicated tables/caching/rate limiting, not additional partitions or buckets

R-SPECIAL-INDEX.desc: JSON array predicates and full-text search must be given a dedicated index contract, including the switch required for existing tables and tokenizer preconditions

R-INPUT-COLLECTION.desc: When requesting quantified inputs, the data-collection SQL must be provided at the same time; do not merely impose a gate

R-DOC-CONFLICT-SPLIT.desc: When official documentation conflicts, split by scenario and state the basis; do not arbitrarily pick one side and turn it into a hard rule

cases.title: Creating tables with each partition type in MySQL mode
cases.input: MySQL mode V4.5.0; separately request HASH / KEY / RANGE / RANGE COLUMNS / LIST partitioned tables

cases.title: Creating tables with each partition type in Oracle mode
cases.input: Oracle mode V4.5.0; request HASH / RANGE / LIST / INTERVAL partitioned tables, where one table has a two-column partition key

cases.title: Oracle mode requests KEY partitioning
cases.input: Oracle mode; the user requests KEY partitioning because the partition key has multiple columns

cases.title: Primary key missing the partition key
cases.input: PARTITION BY HASH(user_id), with the primary key being (order_id)

cases.title: Unique index missing the partition key
cases.input: Partitioned by user_id; email is required to be globally unique

cases.title: Multi-table Table Group + automatic partitioning
cases.input: Two large tables need aligned partitions in the same table group, while also wanting automatic splitting once a threshold is exceeded

cases.title: Sub-partitioned / columnstore table requests automatic partitioning
cases.input: A sub-partitioned table (or columnstore table) requests enabling SIZE

cases.title: Older version requests a new feature
cases.input: Target version V4.2.3; requests automatic partitioning + Table Group SCOPE

cases.title: Using a Hint to route to the columnstore replica
cases.input: The user asks for a Hint to route analytical queries to the columnstore replica

cases.title: Community Edition + Oracle mode
cases.input: edition=community, compat_mode=oracle; requests creating an INTERVAL partitioned table

cases.title: MySQL mode uses VARCHAR as the HASH partition key
cases.input: MySQL mode; requests PARTITION BY HASH(user_code), where user_code is VARCHAR(32)

cases.title: Per-table partition count exceeds the limit (MySQL mode)
cases.input: MySQL mode; requests 200 first-level partitions x 50 sub-partitions = 10000

cases.title: Oracle mode requests RANGE COLUMNS
cases.input: Oracle mode; requests RANGE COLUMNS partitioning on the two columns (tenant_id, stat_date)

cases.title: Oracle mode requests an auto-increment primary key (**must intercept AUTO_INCREMENT**)
cases.input: Enterprise Edition, Oracle mode, V4.5.0; the user requests "make the id column auto-increment as the primary key."

cases.title: Treating a read-hotspot configuration table as a write hotspot (adding a bucket)
cases.input: MySQL mode V4.5.0; a 200-row global configuration table with read_qps=50000, write_qps=2, where the same row is read repeatedly.

cases.title: Columnstore syntax for a pure AP table
cases.input: An offline analytics table with no TP point queries, performing daily multi-dimensional aggregation

cases.title: Low-frequency full-table aggregation
cases.input: A weekly full-table SUM aggregation, scanning 30% of the columns

cases.title: Large table joining a small dictionary table
cases.input: A 1-billion-row order table partitioned by user_id needs to frequently join a 200-row currency dictionary table (the dictionary table has no user_id column)

cases.title: Single-key hotspot
cases.input: A single user_id accounts for 40% of write volume

cases.title: Identifying a queuing table
cases.input: A task table with insert_qps ≈ delete_qps ≈ 2000, a steady-state row count of about 5000, and scans that are gradually slowing down

cases.title: Two high-frequency dimensions conflict
cases.input: An order table needs both point queries by user_id (45%) and aggregation by merchant_id (40%), and both are latency-sensitive

cases.title: Tablet estimation including indexes
cases.input: 3 tables with partition counts of 6/12/1; the first table has 3 local indexes plus 1 global index with 4 partitions

cases.title: Archive table + global index
cases.input: A transaction log table RANGE-partitioned by day and retained for 90 days, which also needs a high-frequency query on a column other than the partition key

cases.title: NOORDER auto-increment column
cases.input: MySQL mode, non-partitioned table, high-concurrency inserts; the business does not require strictly increasing IDs

cases.title: Insufficient input information
cases.input: Only a single sentence is given: "Help me design a user table, the data volume is very large"

cases.title: A partitioned table with neither a primary key nor a unique key must be allowed
cases.input: MySQL mode, a pure append-only tracking table with no primary key and no unique key, RANGE-partitioned by event_time
must_not_include: a partitioned table must have a primary key

cases.title: No primary key but has a unique key
cases.input: No primary key, but has UNIQUE KEY uk(tenant_id, biz_no); partitioned by tenant_id

cases.title: A table with no primary key requests automatic partitioning
cases.input: The no-primary-key table from B11, with an additional request for automatic splitting once a threshold is exceeded

cases.title: Version branching for SHARDING = NONE
cases.input: a) ob_version=4.3.5, two 500GB large tables joining a group with SHARDING=NONE; b) ob_version=4.4.2 BP2, the same request

cases.title: Physical isolation must be able to reach a columnstore replica
cases.input: A pure AP reporting table, isolation_required=yes, OB 4.3.3 + OBProxy 4.3.2 + a dedicated ODP cluster

cases.title: The Tablet limit takes min() and compares on a per-node basis
cases.input: unit_memory_gb=8, unit_num=2, _max_tablet_cnt_per_gb=49999 (50000 is out of range; the valid range [1000,50000) is right-open), total Tablet count 41

cases.title: Auto-increment column used as the partition key
cases.input: The user requests using the auto-increment primary key id directly as the HASH partition key

cases.title: Source of the automatic partitioning threshold
cases.input: The user says: "Just have the table automatically split once it exceeds 30GB, write it into the DDL"

cases.title: A global index is not a forbidden zone
cases.input: A write-heavy, read-light table that has a business number that must be guaranteed unique across partitions

cases.title: The same 10000 partitions must be allowed in Oracle mode
cases.input: Oracle mode; requests 200 first-level partitions x 50 sub-partitions = 10000

cases.title: Unconfirmed capabilities must not enter the main DDL
cases.input: Oracle mode V4.4.2, a transaction log table partitioned by day, requesting automatic partition management

cases.title: A global index's independent partition count must be limited on its own
cases.input: MySQL mode; the main table has 1 partition, but the global index requests 9000 partitions

cases.title: Heterogeneous Zones/Units must assess capacity based on the worst-case node
cases.input: Two units, z1=64GB and z2=1GB, with a total of 30000 Tablets evenly distributed

cases.title: Omitting Column Group when the tenant's default_table_store_format = column
cases.input: MySQL mode V4.5.0, a pure TP order table; the tenant's default_table_store_format has already been set to column.
must_not_include: omitting Column Group means row storage

cases.title: TP-dominant + lightweight AP (four-tier HTAP selection; should not jump straight to row+column redundancy)
cases.input: MySQL mode V4.5.0, a high-frequency point-query order table, plus a once-daily lightweight aggregation report; isolation_required=no.

cases.title: Criteria for upgrading a queuing table's tier (must not explain TABLE_MODE using "queue intensity")
cases.input: MySQL mode V4.5.0, a task queuing table with insert_qps≈delete_qps≈3000 and a steady-state row count of 2000; no measured data on scan degradation is provided.

cases.title: JSON array containment query (must provide a dedicated index, including the switch for existing tables)
cases.input: MySQL mode V4.5.0; the already-live user_info table needs to filter by JSON_CONTAINS(hobbies).

cases.title: The user cannot obtain frequency_share / top1_key_share (must provide the data-collection SQL)
cases.input: The user says: "I can't query the production data, just give me something based on experience for now," but agrees to run a query against the database.

cases.title: No-primary-key columnstore ETL table (two official documents conflict; must be routed by scenario, not rejected)
cases.input: MySQL mode V4.5.0, a pure append-only tracking/analytics table used only for batch import and full-table aggregation; the user explicitly does not want a primary key.
must_not_include: every table must have a primary key

cases.title: Low-cardinality column used for HASH partitioning (NDV < partition count -- legal DDL, defective design)
cases.input: MySQL mode V4.5.0; the status column has only 6 distinct values, and the user requests PARTITION BY HASH(status) PARTITIONS 128.
